CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KRISHNA S.DIXIT  AND  THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL)

These two appeals are filed by the claimants/injured seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by common judgment and award dated 4.7.2019 passed in MVC No.2027/2018 & 2029/2018 on the file of learned IV Addl. District Judge and MACT-V, Belagavi1.

2. Brief facts leading to filing of these appeals are that, the claimants/injured filed claim petitions before the Tribunal seeking compensation for the accidental injuries sustained on 28.02.2018 involving Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-22/EM-0089 and Maruti Swift Car bearing registration No.MH-18/W-8136.
Due to the accident, they suffered permanent physical disability.
Both claimants were aged about 24 years at the time of the accident, were doing masonry work and earning Rs.15,000/- per month. 'Tribunal' for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:11658-DB 3.
On appearance, respondent No.3/Insurance Company has filed a statement of objections denying the claim petition averments.
It was contended that the rider of the motorcycle as well as the driver of the offending car were not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Thus, sought dismissal of the claim petitions.

4. The Tribunal on scrutiny of entire material available on record allowed the claim petitions in part awarding a total compensation of Rs.15,38,381/- in MVC No.2027/2018 and Rs.6,28,939/- in MVC No.2029/2018 with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petitions till realization.
Aggrieved by the same, both claimants/injured are in appeal.
5. Learned counsel Sri. Yash R Nadkarni for the appellants/injured submits that in MVC No.2027/2018, the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the disability of the injured.

He submits that PW3-doctor has assessed the disability of the injured-Narayan at 40% and PW4-doctor has assessed disability at 50%, hence, the injured is entitled to compensation under the head of loss of future prospects.

It is also submitted that the Tribunal has further committed an error in assessing the income of the injured at Rs.8,500/- per month, NC: 2024:KHC-D:11658-DB which is on the lower side, as he was doing masonry work and earning more than Rs.15,000/- per month.

sentences.text: 6. It is further submitted that in MVC No.2029/2018, the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the injured at Rs.8,500/- per month, which is on the lesser side.
He further submits that the Tribunal has assessed the disability of the injured-Vijay at 20%, which is contrary to the evidence of doctor, who assessed the disability of the injured at 55%.
He also submits that the award of compensation by the Tribunal under all other heads is on the lower side and seeks to re-assess the same appropriately by allowing the appeal.
7. Per contra, learned counsel Sri. G.N. Raichur for respondent/Insurer submits that the award of compensation by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not call for enhancement.
He further submits that both the claimants were working as masons and the disability suffered by them would not come in the way of their masonry work.
Hence, there is no need to award compensation towards loss of future NC: 2024:KHC-D:11658-DB prospects.
He further submits that the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of both the injured in the absence of any cogent and acceptable evidence on record.
Therefore, he seeks to sustain the same and prays to dismiss both the appeals.
8. I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record including original records of the Tribunal.
9. The evidence and pleadings on record indicates that both the claimants met with road accident on 28.2.2018 and sustained grievous injuries.
The claim petition indicates that both were working as Masons and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
However, no evidence whatsoever is placed on record with regard to the income of the injured.
Hence, this Court re- assesses the income of both the injured notionally at Rs.11,750/- per month placing reliance on notional income chart prepared by KSLSA.
10. Insofar as disability is concerned, in MVC No.2027/2018, the Tribunal assessed the disability of the injured-Narayan at 60%.

On re-appreciation of oral evidence of PW3 and PW4 and considering the Disability Certificate, NC: 2024:KHC-D:11658-DB Discharge Summary and other medical evidence on record, we are of the considered view that the Tribunal has rightly assessed disability,
which is unaltered.

Thus, loss of future earnings due to disability is reckoned as under:
Rs.11750 x 12 x 18 x 60/100 = Rs.15,22,800/-
11.

Taking note of the fact that the claimant was inpatient for a period of 21 days, treatment provided to him and loss of vision of left eye, we modify the compensation as under:
 Pain and suffering Rs. 1,00,000/-
 Medical expenses Rs. 2,58,281/-
Loss of future earnings due to disability Rs.15,22,800/- Food, nourishment, attendant and Transportation charges Rs. 30,000/-

Thus, the claimant in MVC No.2027/2018 is entitled to total compensation of Rs.20,18,081/- as against Rs.15,38,381/- awarded by the Tribunal.

13. In MVC No.2029/2018, the claimant-Vijay was aged about 24 years at the time of accident and he has sustained fracture of pelvic bone, C-7 Vertebra, Undisplaced fracture of right fibula head and fracture of right 2nd metatarsal bone.
Taking note of said fractures and keeping in mind the oral testimony of PW3-doctor, we re-assess the disability of the injured-Vijay at 22% as against 20% assessed by the Tribunal.

Thus, loss of future earnings due to disability is recalculated as under:
Rs.11,750 x 12 x 18 x 22% = Rs.5,58,360/-
14.

Taking note of oral testimony of PW3 and PW4 and also keeping in mind that the injured was an inpatient for about 20 days, we re-assess the compensation as under:
 Pain and suffering Rs. 75,000/-
 Medical expenses Rs.1,30,239/-
Loss of future earnings due to disability Rs.5,58,360/- Food, nourishment, attendant and Transportation charges Rs. 30,000/-
Loss of income during laid-up period Rs. 47,000/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
Thus, the claimant in MVC No.2029/2018 is entitled to total compensation of Rs.8,90,599/- as against Rs.6,28,939/- awarded by the Tribunal.

16. In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER a) Both appeals stand partly allowed.

5 b) The impugned common judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the claimant in MVC No.2027/2018 is entitled to total compensation of Rs.20,18,081/- as against Rs.15,38,381/- awarded by the Tribunal and the claimant in MVC No.2029/2018 is entitled to total compensation of Rs.8,90,599/- as against Rs.6,28,939/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petitions till realization.

d) The respondent/Insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount in both appeals with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) Apportionment, deposit & disbursement shall be made in terms of award of Tribunal.
f) TCR be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.
